title: Use a process diagram to show the steps an institution takes to decide, and where others can step in.
rule: Number the steps of the main path, as the law lays them out, and run them down one heavy line in order, each in a box with an edge in the text’s ink that names the step, who acts and the time the law sets. Keep the steps one even gap apart, since distance along the line reads as time, and set each branch a case may take in a column beside them, starting level with the step it leaves or enters, in a box with a gray edge and a short line that says when it applies, joined by a gray arrow (Rule 14.6); arrows on the main line point the way a case moves. Print the date of the law the diagram draws, and give the table every step and branch in the order a reader meets them, each with where it leads. On a phone the steps run in one column, a step’s way in above it and its branches below it, set in from the line.
use_when: The reader asks how an institution makes or changes something, such as how an agency writes a rule, and where Congress, a court or the public can step in.

use_instead.when: One bill or rule’s place in its steps is the question
The reader picks a path by answering questions about their own place
The question is how long each step can take for one person

text: One line through the main path lets a reader learn it first, and the branches beside it show where the path can turn without hiding it. Numbers keep the order when the diagram is read aloud or as a table.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form process-diagram: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s66; encode.path marks the main steps with labels.main, labels.branches gives each branch the step it leaves or enters (at), its way (dir, out or in) and its line of words, and the table sorts by encode.key’s values in reading order.
